title: Encode/Decode: from core dialog to the encoder add-on
description: The encode/decode tool as recorded in the zaproxy and zap-extensions histories: a core extension in the first import, an add-on from 2018, and the core classes' deprecation and removal.
narrative:
Developers and testers often need a quick encode or decode step while they work, so it is easy to see why a proxy would keep that step close at hand. The first commit, titled Version 1.0.0 in September 2010, already contained an encoder dialog and the older encoder classes. Core commits kept changing the dialog, including a 2014 change to support HTML and JavaScript encoding.

In October 2018 a zap-extensions commit added an Advanced Encoder Decoder add-on. Work on it continued into May 2020. In May 2020 the add-on was moved to a new encoder directory and given a new add-on ID. The encoder changelog's first entry, 0.1.0, is marked First version. Version 0.2.0 in June 2020 added Base64 character set and line break options, and migrated settings from the core component.

In May 2020 a core commit deprecated the encoder2 classes, noting that weekly builds now included the add-on. In February 2021 a commit deleted Base64.java, Encoder.java and the encoder2 classes. Its body said the removal was part of the 2.11 milestone.

The add-on was promoted to Beta in December 2020. The 1.0.0 release in December 2022 promoted it to Release status. It also carried a breaking change to the script process method signature. A PowerShell encoder arrived in March 2023. Morse Code processors and ASCify followed in January 2025. The add-on is at release status. Its most recent entry named here is a resizable input area in March 2026.

chapters.title: Encoder classes in the first core import
chapters.text: The zaproxy commit titled "Version 1.0.0" (2010-09-04) contains org/parosproxy/paros/extension/encoder/ExtensionEncoder.java and Encoder.java, plus org/zaproxy/zap/extension/encoder2/EncodeDecodeDialog.java. Both the older encoder package and the encoder2 package are therefore present from the earliest commit in the clone.

chapters.title: Core encoder2 keeps changing
chapters.text: Core commits touching the encode/decode dialog include "Issue 1012: 	Encode / Decode dialog - support HTML and JavaScript encoding / decoding" (2014-03-03) and "Add Base64url to Encoder/Decoder Tool" (2019-10-28).

chapters.title: An Advanced Encoder Decoder add-on appears in zap-extensions
chapters.text: On 2018-10-31 the zap-extensions commit "Implemented new Extension Advanced Encoder Decoder" adds addOns/advancedencoder with a CHANGELOG.md and advancedencoder.gradle.kts. The commit "Add reset button, fix title caps, fix JS template" (2020-05-13) is one of several that continue that add-on before it was renamed.

chapters.title: Renamed to encoder and released as 0.1.0
chapters.text: On 2020-05-18 the commit "New addonID and paths" moves addOns/advancedencoder to addOns/encoder (CHANGELOG.md is a rename and the Gradle file becomes encoder.gradle.kts). The encoder CHANGELOG records "## [0.1.0] - 2020-05-20" with the line "First version.", then 0.2.0 (2020-06-01) with "Base64 character set and line break options, including migration of settings from core component."

chapters.title: Core classes deprecated, then removed
chapters.text: On 2020-05-27 the zaproxy commit "encoder2: Deprecate and address dependence" has a body saying "CoreFunctionality > Remove encoder2 from core, weekly is now including addon from zap-extensions." and touches the encoder and encoder2 classes (3 lines added in Base64 and 2 in Encoder). On 2021-02-02 the commit "encoder: Remove deprecated classes" deletes Base64.java, Encoder.java and the encoder2 classes; its body reads "Remove deprecated code, part of 2.11 milestone."

chapters.title: Beta in 2020, release in 2022, current state
chapters.text: The CHANGELOG records "Promoted to Beta." in 0.4.0 (2020-12-15) and, in 1.0.0 (2022-12-15), "Add-on promoted to Release status." together with a BREAKING CHANGE note about the script process method signature. Later entries include a PowerShell encoder (1.1.0, 2023-03-13), Morse Code processors and ASCify (1.6.0, 2025-01-09) and a resizable input area (1.9.0, 2026-03-02). The add-on status in the dataset is release.
